insights: n8n.io's own workflow template marketplace is a major existing competitor for this exact use case: it lists ~598 social-media automation workflows and dozens of free templates directly matching the pipeline (e.g. 'AI-powered news monitoring & social post generator with OpenAI and Upload-Post', 'Auto-publish web articles as social posts for X, LinkedIn, Reddit & Threads with Gemini AI'). Any paid landing page must differentiate on done-for-you setup, reliability, and support, not on 'n8n can do this.'

Standard architecture across competitor workflows: RSS/Google Trends/Perplexity for source discovery -> OpenAI/Gemini/GPT-4 for content writing -> Airtable/Google Sheets as a content-calendar/review layer -> Buffer, Upload-Post, or Postiz (or native platform APIs) for scheduling/publishing across platforms. This discover -> enrich -> review -> schedule -> publish model is the mental model prospects expect the page to address.

Cost positioning is a strong differentiator: n8n bills per workflow execution rather than per step/task, which agencies use to pitch dramatically cheaper automation at scale versus Zapier (one case cited reducing a Zapier bill from $3,000/month to $80/month on n8n, with 3-4 month payback periods).

Common People-Also-Ask style questions in this space: 'n8n vs Zapier vs Make' comparisons, 'how much does n8n cost', 'how much time does content automation save', and 'what's the ROI/payback period of marketing automation' -- these are natural FAQ/PAA sections for the page.

Agency/service pricing benchmarks for n8n automation builds: fixed project pricing around $5,000 for a workshop plus up to 4 production automations, or retainers of roughly $1,000-$2,500/month; project-only engagements often run 4-6 weeks flat fee.

Time-savings claims vary widely by source (from ~3 hours per piece of content to 13 hours/week overall for marketers using AI), so the page should use a conservative, defensible range rather than the highest cited number to stay credible.

insights: The workflow splits the Apify scraping step into two separate n8n workflows (scrape, then a wait-for-finish webhook workflow) specifically because Apify's default wait time is only 60 seconds, which causes timeouts on larger scraping jobs.

Content ideas are filtered in two layers: a hard numeric filter (minimum 2,000 views) followed by an AI (ChatGPT) classification step checking language, topical relevance, and 'virality' before an idea is added to the Google Sheet.

The pipeline uses a Google Apps Script + onEdit trigger (rather than a native n8n Google Sheets trigger) to turn the spreadsheet into a webhook-triggered app, firing into n8n only when specific checkbox columns (column I = generate, column J = post) are set to true, to avoid accidentally triggering generation/publishing on every edit.
Google Sheets API is rate-limited to 300 requests per minute, which is why the workflow loops through items one at a time with a 5-second delay between each rather than batch processing.

Blotato, the multi-platform posting tool used, costs roughly $30-40/month and requires manually built HTTP request nodes (POST with Content-Type: application/json plus a Blotato API key) since n8n has no native Blotato integration node.
A free alternative to paying for Blotato mentioned in the video is routing the publishing step through Make.com instead.

Before uploading to social platforms, the Google Drive image file's sharing permission must be changed to 'anyone with the link' (reader), otherwise the platforms can't fetch and publish a privately-shared image.
JSON.stringify() is applied to caption text before sending it to the Blotato API specifically to strip line breaks and quotation marks so the payload conforms to JSON formatting requirements.

The creator layers a lead-gen tactic on top of the auto-posting system: asking viewers to comment for a free resource, then DMing them a Notion page containing the blueprint, used as a growth/personal-branding mechanism alongside the automation.
